purpose: held-out evaluation for prediction and confusion sets; NOT used to train the bigram model

disjointness.proven_by: scripts/build_eval_corpus.py refuses to write when any eval byte range intersects a training byte range

known_limitations: Wikipedia prose; the register is wrong for phone typing.
Sentence splitting is punctuation-based and will merge or split some sentences.

sample.used_by: M10 prediction: the weight sweep, the ordering sweep, and the locked accuracy floors.

slices.why: The full corpus is 28 MB and is not committed; these deterministic slices are what the tests read. Re-cut them with scripts/slice_eval_corpus.py after rebuilding the corpus.
slices.rule: strided slices: sentences of 4..40 tokens, every 37th from a per-slice offset, first 6000. Block slices: 120 contiguous blocks of 80 sentences each, drawn from the sentences the strided slices left unused.
slices.proven_by: scripts/slice_eval_corpus.py compares the index sets and refuses to write when any two slices intersect

sample.used_by: M10 prediction: the weight sweep, the ordering sweep, and the locked accuracy floors.

confusion_dev.used_by: M11 real-word errors: the margin sweep. Thresholds are chosen here and nowhere else.

confusion_test.used_by: M11 real-word errors: the reported recall and false-alarm numbers, measured once with the thresholds already fixed.

learning_dev.used_by: Adaptive learning: the interpolation sweep and the cold-start curve. Thresholds are chosen here and nowhere else.

learning_test.used_by: Adaptive learning: the reported top-1/top-3 and offer rates, measured once with the interpolation already fixed.

conversational_test.register: transcribed dialogue -- NOT written phone messages, which no corpus here contains. A better proxy than an encyclopedia, and nothing more.
conversational_test.used_by: R1: every claim about conversational-register accuracy.
conversational_test.disjoint_from_training_by: construction -- build_subtitle_corpus.py writes each sentence to exactly one of train / held-out
